key_insight: The paper argues that AI/ML in turbulence modeling works best when deployment is matched to the flow’s regime, using a complexity-based map in degrees of freedom and non-equilibrium to decide between ML-RANS, SRS, and PINNs.
engineering_relevance: For practical CFD, this framework helps engineers avoid using expensive scale-resolving methods where RANS suffices and avoid overextending ML closures beyond the flow conditions they were trained on.
method: Build a turbulence taxonomy map using Reynolds number and non-equilibrium measure (SK/ε).
Apply Weaver’s complexity framework to separate turbulence into distinct physical regimes.
Match modeling choice to regime: ML-RANS for locally generalizable closures, SRS where explicit resolution is necessary, and PINNs where physics constraints add value.
evidence_signal: The abstract presents a conceptual, regime-based assessment rather than new benchmark data, arguing from known failure modes of ML-RANS and cost limits of SRS.
watch_item: The taxonomy is only useful if the regime boundaries are estimated reliably in real flows; misclassification could still lead to poor model choice or invalid extrapolation.
paper_title: AI Meets Turbulence Modeling: Complex Systems Perspective
